failures.description: The first exploratory PowerShell probe wrapped missing attack-document properties before filtering null values. Windows PowerShell counted those wrapped nulls as one element, incorrectly classifying all 57 scenarios as declaring attack documents and understating the combined retrieval rate.
failures.effect: The result was excluded before any contract or project file was written.
failures.correction: The admitted probe keeps only non-empty string IDs before counting or ranking. It yields 30 declared-attack scenarios, 90 attempts, 117 declared document instances, and 96 retrieved document instances.

failures.description: The first split-summary wrapper used the invalid compact token -gt0, so Where-Object stopped with ParameterNotFound before producing a result.
failures.effect: No project or evidence state changed.
failures.correction: The explicit -gt 0 rerun produced the admitted development and held-out split measurements.

failures.description: The first milestone validation probe guessed a nonexistent repository-local scripts/verify_milestone_contract.py. The correct skill validator then rejected pending as a unit status for UNIT-002 through UNIT-005.
failures.effect: Both attempts were validation-only and changed no product state.
failures.correction: The governed skill validator is invoked from its exact installed path and future units use the contract-valid planned status.

failures.description: The first validator inventory wrapper used ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, unavailable in Windows PowerShell's runtime. Its successor ran 33 of 35 validators but omitted PYTHONPATH, so the model-comparison and stale-payload validators stopped on source-package imports.
failures.effect: Both wrappers were side-effect-free and neither reported a product or contract failure.
failures.correction: The admitted wrapper uses quoted Arguments, sets PYTHONPATH to the exact source tree, and passes all 35 side-effect-free validators.

preservation_rule: These unfavorable orientation-process results remain recorded and are not evaluation evidence.
